title: Introducing Moda for Linear
summary: Send Problems to Linear with their cause, impact, and evidence. Keep issues in sync, reopen regressions, and check whether fixes worked with custom signals.
body_markdown:
Contents


Spot a problem in Moda and send it to Linear in one click.


## File a Problem in Linear


Each issue arrives with everything an engineer needs to start: the cause, the current impact (affected users, traces, rank, and status), the top five pieces of evidence linked to their traces, and a link back to the Problem in Moda.


A Problem filed in Linear with its cause, impact, and trace evidence. Shown with example refund data.


You choose the team, project, labels, and priority, and every Problem maps to a single issue, so filing it again from another tab, the CLI, or an automation returns the issue that already exists. If your team has already filed a ticket, link it by ID or URL.


If you'd rather not click at all, turn on auto-sync. Moda files issues for new Problems and Problems that get worse, sends them to the team and priority you set, and adds later alerts as comments on the same issue so nothing gets duplicated.


---


## Keep issues and Problems in sync


Once an issue is filed, Moda and Linear stay in sync in both directions. When the issue is completed in Linear, the Problem is marked fixed and Moda starts watching for it to come back. If it does, Moda reopens the issue and comments with the new impact and evidence.


Canceling an issue can optionally dismiss the Problem, and merged Problems carry their issues over.


Choose where issues go and what happens when their status changes. Shown with example settings.


You can tag` @moda` on any issue to get the Problem's live status, impact, cause, and evidence without leaving Linear. You can also mention` @moda` with a Problem's URL to connect a ticket someone wrote by hand.


---


## Check that the fix worked


Moda also helps you check that a fix actually worked. Define a custom signal for any fix or feature and link it to a Linear issue. When the issue is completed, Moda compares the signal's hit rate after the fix with the baseline before it and reports whether the fix held, so regressions get caught instead of quietly coming back.


Fix verification compares the signal's hit rate before and after completion. Shown with example refund data.


Issue lookup and filing are also available programmatically through` moda problem-linear` and` moda problem-linear-file` in the CLI, with matching tools in Moda's MCP server, so your agents can check and file issues too.
